newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy rail chief arrested in corruption probe-media.
newsitem.headline: Italy rail chief arrested in corruption probe-media.

text.p: Police have arrested the managing director of Italy's state railway system, Lorenzo Necci, in an investigation into suspected embezzlement of railway funds, media reports quoting judicial sources said on Monday.
Necci, 55, has been overseeing a plan to launch a multi-billion dollar high-speed railway which, when it gets off the ground, is expected to be one of Europe's biggest construction projects.
Italian television and news agencies said Necci had been arrested on Sunday on a warrant from magistrates in the northwest coastal town of La Spezia and was being held in jail there.
A spokesman for the railway, Ferrovie dello Stato, declined to comment until magistrates had publicly confirmed the arrest.
The magistrates told reporters in La Spezia they were conducting a probe involving the railway, but made no further comment.

News agencies AGI and ANSA, quoting judicial sources, said Necci was being held on suspicion of offences which included criminal association, corruption, abuse of office, money laundering, false accounting, fraud and embezzlement.
Two businessmen and a secretary had also been arrested in the investigation on similar charges, they reported.

ANSA said the magistrates were probing suspected embezzlement of funds from the railroad and its subsidiaries, adding that the investigation also was looking into a Swiss bank account held by one of the businessmen.
Trade union leaders who worked closely with Necci said they were worried about how Necci's arrest would affect the high-speed project.
"A vacuum in leadership at this phase could be fatal to the soundness of the company," said Walter Cerfeda, a top official of the CGIL trades union grouping.
"I'm shocked," said Paolo Brutti, secretary general of the FILT-CIGL union representing railway workers.
"For the unions, Necci's arrest was a surprise, but also the source of great worry for the launch of major works on the railway infrastructure and the modernisation of the system."
The agencies said the magistrates would interview Necci in jail on Tuesday or Wednesday.
